name: Église Saint-Merri
note: In the outer ring (beyond the box): its fringe building is replaced. West front on the Rue Saint-Martin.

name: Musée Carnavalet — the court
note: Standalone in the court between the U's arms of OSM's way 57832953; −z toward the entrance wing and the Rue de Sévigné (ESE). The corps de logis at the head of the court is drawn by the model — OSM leaves that end open.

name: Hôtel de Soubise — the cour d’honneur
note: The horseshoe colonnade court and the palace front, in the building's courtyard; the gate end toward the Rue des Francs-Bourgeois (south).

name: Hôtel de Sully — the court
note: Drawn on the building's own courtyard; the building (OSM relation 403146, stone-dressed by the hôtels-particuliers restyle) stays.

name: Colonne de Juillet
note: A monument: its column is not a building in OSM, but its base is mapped as three building parts (78271167, 227757687, 227757691) which the generated city would draw as a glass box round the foot of the column — so they are replaced too, and it stands at its own coordinates.

name: Centre Pompidou
note: The piazza front faces WNW, square to the building's long axis (21° east of north). With front 270 the fit measured the rotated footprint across a north–south box: the model came out oversized and turned, through its neighbours and over the street.

name: Église Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis
note: The facade faces Rue Saint-Antoine (NNE). Not 'street': the baked frontage is the longest street-facing wall, which for this church is its east flank on Rue Saint-Paul.

name: Hôtel de Sens
note: Front on the Rue du Figuier (bearing 62°): the turrets and the gateway face it, not the Rue de l'Hôtel de Ville the frontage rule picked (BUGS.md #7).

name: Tour Saint-Jacques
note: Standalone, outside the box: nothing in the package to replace. The model includes its square (lawn, paths, trees).

name: Tour Saint-Jacques — OSM footprint
note: Placeholder: removes OSM's own 52 m tower (a fringe building, drawn as dark 'skyscraper' massing inside the model — BUGS.md #5). The model is placed by lat/lon above.

name: Hôtel de Ville
note: Main front west onto the Place; the rider mostly sees the east (back) and south fronts, so the back has its pavilions too. The ways after the relation are its courtyard wings, mapped separately with their centres inside the outline; the model covers them.

name: Place des Vosges
note: Every house fronting the square (the Square Louis-XIII's garden, as a rectangle; a building is taken if a corner is within 16 m of it) takes the brick-and-stone style, two storeys over the arcade (eaves 14 m) and a steep 8 m slate roof, as the real pavilions have — OSM's heights of 16–20 m include the roofs. 16 m takes 55 — 14 missed the Hôtel de Chaulnes (no. 9), whose front stands 15 m from the garden; 10 takes none (the street round the garden is ~12 m).

name: Opéra Bastille — the curved foyers
note: The colossal curved wall of glass round the foyers, facing the Place: the two parts of the curve (aerial), glazed whole, ahead of the restyle below, which dresses the rest in white granite.

name: Opéra Bastille
note: OSM maps the Opéra as 61 parts with real heights — the 50 m stage house, the stepped terraces of the curved front — so the massing is kept and only the dress changes: every part whose centre is inside the outline (way/78149064, simplified to 3 m) takes the granite-and-glass grid style with a flat roof. The parts that start above the ground — the stepped tiers of the curved front — take the pale glass curtain instead, and the blocks that stand on the ground the white granite: the building's black-and-white look (Street View, May 2018).

name: Opéra Bastille — the arch
note: Standalone, where OSM maps it (the 15 m parts 255526605/606 and the 2.5 m steps 255526607/608, removed by the placeholder below), facing north-west to the Place. The building itself is the restyle entry above.

name: Opéra Bastille — arch parts
note: Placeholder: removes OSM's arch and steps, which the procedural arch replaces.

name: Synagogue de la rue Pavée
note: Hector Guimard, 1913. The baked frontage is the rue Pavée front (WNW).

name: Synagogue de la rue des Tournelles
note: Varcollier, 1876. The baked frontage is the rue des Tournelles front (east).

name: Square Louis-XIII
note: The garden inside the Place des Vosges, at the centre of the park rectangle, turned 13.8° with it (the rectangle's sides run at 13.8°). Size is only the shadow's footprint: the statue's, not the garden's.

name: Temple du Marais
note: Temple Sainte-Marie (François Mansart, 1632), 17 rue Saint-Antoine — on the south side of the street, so its porch faces north. Not 'street': the baked frontage is its flank. The ways after the first are its drum, dome and porch, mapped as parts inside the outline; they drew through the model.

name: Église Saint-Gervais
note: The classical front faces west, onto the Place Saint-Gervais behind the Hôtel de Ville; the baked frontage is the south flank.

name: Cirque d'Hiver
note: Hittorff, 1852. OSM's outline was replaced by this part; placed at the landmark's own point, entrance to the west (rue des Filles-du-Calvaire).

name: Église Saint-Denys-du-Saint-Sacrement
note: Godde, 1835: the Ionic portico faces west onto the rue de Turenne.

name: Hôtels particuliers
note: The Marais's 17th-century mansions — Sully, Soubise, Lamoignon, Rohan, Carnavalet and seventy more named in OSM — wear pale dressed stone and a steep slate roof instead of the neighbourhood's random mix. The Hôtel de Ville and the Hôtel de Sens have models of their own and are excluded by the regular expression's position (they are replaced, so not restyled).

name: Saint-Louis-en-l'Île — spire and clock
note: On the church (OSM's parts 330517677/330517682 are its massing), 6 m in from the frontage on the Rue Saint-Louis-en-l'Île; facing the street (29°) so the clock hangs out over it. Lifted to the 24 m roofline.

name: Tour Eiffel
note: At its own point, square to the Champ de Mars (faces NE–SW / NW–SE). Its OSM outline (330 m) and parts are removed by the placeholder below; the small pavilions at its foot stay.

name: Tour Eiffel — OSM outline and parts
note: Placeholder: OSM's tower drawn as a 330 m windowed block and its stacked parts.

name: Arc de Triomphe
note: Fitted to OSM's attic outline (way 226413514, 45 × 22 m), its front (the −z face) down the Champs-Élysées; every OSM part of the arch replaced.

name: Palais du Louvre
note: Drawn wing by wing on OSM's outline and IGN's aerial (2026-10-30), in plan metres about this point: not fitted, and on its own datum, because the ground runs from -3 m in the Colonnade's moat to +2.4 in the Cour Carrée and an entry's base is otherwise the lowest of it. OSM's outline stays in the bake for the passages' vaults (TileData.claimedBuildings).

name: Tours Société Générale
note: Alicante and Chassagne, La Défense (owner, 2026-10-30, 48.891995, 2.230358: "colors are not quite right"): OSM has them as pale glass, building:facade:colour #A2E1FA, where the office towers' palette is dark. A silvery glass from the styles there are; not their own colour.

name: Louvre Pyramid
note: Pei's pyramid in the Cour Napoléon on OSM way 375076234's outline, square to the palace (bearing 109.4, 6° off the historic axis), with the three small pyramids where OSM's ways 53815259–61 have them. All four ways replaced (they drew as a glass box and two small generic buildings). The court's ground is levelled by regions.json's `levelGrounds`, the basins are OSM's water.

name: Notre-Dame
note: Fitted to OSM's whole-plan part (way 201611267), the west front toward the parvis; every OSM part of the cathedral and its duplicating relation (packed 13103927) replaced.

name: Dôme des Invalides
note: The church and its dome: the middle of the dome off IGN's aerial, front to the Place Vauban. OSM's church (way 112452790 and its parts) goes, and with it its block of windows.

name: Musée d'Orsay
note: The Gare d'Orsay, on OSM's outline turned to its true bearing (25.5°, off the outline's long side): front to the Seine.

name: Palais Garnier
note: On the middle of OSM's main footprint (way 822291002) at its true size: fitted to the outline the loader gave it 10 m across, which the old clamps hid and a drawing in real metres cannot. Front to the Place de l'Opéra (south-south-east); OSM's dome, stage and wing parts replaced.

name: Place de la Concorde
note: The obelisk at the midpoint of OSM's two pools, the fountains in them (64 m either side, the axis 25.7° east of north), the rostral columns; OSM's 0.3 m obelisk base replaced.

name: Monument à la République
note: The pedestal: platform, drum with its bronze frieze, the three seated allegories, the shaft; Marianne and the lion are the user's models attached to it (paris-statues.json). Facing (225°) to be checked against a photograph.

name: Danton — OSM plinth
note: Placeholder: OSM maps Danton's plinth as a 4 m building; the statue pool builds the pedestal.

name: Palais de Chaillot
note: The two head pavilions and the two curved galleries of 1937, on OSM's outline: on its own datum, the parvis, because the north-east wing's ground falls 20 m from it; the parvis and its gilded statues are `trocaderoParvis`.

name: Parvis du Trocadéro
note: The eight gilded figures and the balustrade over the gardens; the axis points at the Eiffel Tower.

name: Grand Palais
note: The glass nave and dome on green iron, the colonnade to the Avenue Winston-Churchill, the quadrigas; fitted to OSM's outline, front to the avenue (east). Sized inside the Avenue du Général-Eisenhower (north) and the Cours la Reine: the outline's 240 m rectangle stood over the avenue the ride goes along (BUGS.md #43). OSM maps it as eight building:parts, all replaced.

name: Colonne Vendôme
note: The bronze Trajan's column: pedestal and eagles, the spiral frieze, gallery, lantern, Napoleon; OSM's three column parts replaced.

name: Sainte-Chapelle
note: The glass chapel: lancets between pinnacled buttresses, the apse, the steep lead roof with its gilded cresting and spire, the west rose and turrets; OSM's 75 m block and its parts replaced.

name: Église de la Madeleine
note: The Corinthian temple: 52 columns on the podium, the Last Judgement pediment, the front down the Rue Royale; OSM's 63 parts (cella, steps, columns) replaced — drawn as buildings they made a windowed tower.

name: Assemblée nationale — portico
note: The Palais Bourbon's twelve-column portico and pediment to the Seine, standing on its quai front; the palace behind is OSM's massing. Moved 2026-10-29 onto OSM's own portico parts (w380420446 steps, w1459531653 colonnade), facing the Concorde–Madeleine axis at 25.6°: it stood 39 m west facing due north, beside the real one the palaces' Bourbon restyle dresses.

name: Institut de France
note: Le Vau's hemicycle on the Quai de Conti: OSM's 30 m massing brought down to its real 17 m in the classical stone dress; the chapel front and dome are `institutDome`. Slate on it (Batch 1, 2026-10-31: tan flat roofs from the Pont des Arts, where the aerial has slate).

name: Institut de France — dome
note: The portico to the quai, the drum with its paired pilasters, the ribbed lead dome with gilded ribs, the lantern.

name: Petit Palais
note: The Ionic colonnade, the great arched entrance with its gilded gate, the ribbed dome; front to the Avenue Winston-Churchill (west).

name: Colonnes de Buren
note: Les Deux Plateaux: ~260 black-and-white striped octagonal columns on a grid across the Cour d'Honneur, stepping in height.

name: Palais-Royal — galleries
note: The arcaded stone galleries round the garden and the Cour d'Honneur (Valois, Montpensier, Beaujolais) in place of generic Haussmann shopfronts.

name: École Militaire
note: Gabriel's building on the Champ de Mars: the main block in the classical stone dress under slate; its square dome is OSM's own part, the portico `ecoleMilitairePortico`.

name: École Militaire — portico
note: The central frontispiece: ten Corinthian columns over two storeys and the pediment, to the Champ de Mars.

name: Rue de Rivoli — arcades
note: Percier and Fontaine's uniform arcaded fronts along the Tuileries, from the Concorde to the Louvre: stone, arcades at street level, the mansard over.

name: Place Vendôme — facades
note: Hardouin-Mansart's uniform facades round the octagonal place: arcaded ground floor, giant pilasters, mansard with dormers.

name: Fontaine des Innocents
note: Goujon's Renaissance pavilion on its cascading steps, in the square at Les Halles.

name: Fontaine Saint-Michel
note: Davioud's triumphal-arch wall fountain closing the Place Saint-Michel, the archangel over the devil, dragons, red columns.

name: Flamme de la Liberté
note: The gilded flame on its black granite plinth above the Alma tunnel.

name: Hôtel de la Marine and Hôtel de Crillon
note: Gabriel's twin palaces on the north side of the Concorde, drawn in plan metres about the obelisk: the Marine, and the Crillon with the Plessis-Bellière and Coislin behind one front.

name: La Conciergerie
note: The front on the Quai de l'Horloge: the Horloge, César and Argent, the Bonbec, the ranges between; the Palais de Justice's OSM parts along the quay give way to it.

name: Palais de Justice — the tall parts
note: The Palais stands four tall storeys, not a seven-storey hotel on the Quai de l'Horloge west of the Bonbec: OSM's parts (24-30 m to their ridges, storeys guessed) named one by one, as the massing of a restyle by relation does not reach them (render/landmarks.ts `styleOnly`). PARIS_BUGS: the top 25's Palais de Justice.

name: Palais de Justice and the Conciergerie
note: The Palais de Justice on the Île de la Cité, OSM's parts in pale stone; the Conciergerie's quay front is its own model, above, and takes the parts it stands on first.

name: Hôtel de la Monnaie
note: The Mint on the Quai de Conti, beside the Institut: a long plain classical front with its projecting centre. Slate on it (Batch 1, 2026-10-31).

name: Place des Victoires — facades
note: Hardouin-Mansart's uniform facades round the round place.

name: Rue Royale
note: The uniform fronts of the Rue Royale between the Concorde and the Madeleine.

name: Louis XIV — Place des Victoires
note: Stand-in for the user's model (MODELS_NEEDED.md): the rearing horseman on his pedestal in the middle of the place.

name: Foch — Place du Trocadéro
note: Stand-in for the user's model (MODELS_NEEDED.md): Foch on horseback, facing the Eiffel Tower.

name: Beside the Sacré-Cœur: a lodge
note: A 14 by 4 m lodge east of the basilica, no height in OSM, that took 50 m from the lidar's reading of the basilica over it: from the terraces it stood as a tower with the Sacré-Cœur's own height (top-25 audit, 2026-10-30).
